nodes.name: Ni50Cu50 bimetallic carbonization
nodes.procedure: 1.5 g of Cu(NO3)2·2.5H2O and 1.5 g of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O were added into a 100 mL beaker and dissolved in 10 mL of DI water. Afterward, 3.0 g of tissue paper were dipped into the salt solution and the mixture was bath sonicated so that all the metal ions (Cu²⁺ and Ni²⁺) were adsorbed on the surface of the tissue paper. The tissue paper was then heated to 100°C to remove all the water. Subsequently, the tissue papers were carbonized in a tube furnace at 700°C. High purity argon gas was passed through the tube furnace to remove air for at least 1 h prior to the carbonization process. The heating rate of the carbonization was set as 5°C min⁻¹. The process was carried out in a high-purity argon atmosphere. The sample was carbonized for 3 h in a quartz boat.

nodes.name: Acid etching purification
nodes.procedure: The carbonized product was taken out once the temperature reached room temperature and the product was then dispersed in a 1.0 M sulfuric acid solution with the assistance of ultrasonication to remove any unstable metallic substances. The etching process was performed for 24 h. The product was collected by centrifugation and washed for several times using DI water. The obtained product was then brought to neutral pH and vacuum-dried at 70°C for 12 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu/C bimetallic nanoparticles show FCC structure with (111), (200), and (220) crystal planes with slight peak shift compared to Cu/C and Ni/C; highest lattice contraction observed in Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD analysis of the NiCu/C bimetallic nanoparticles also showed a similar diffraction pattern with a slight shift compared to the Cu and Ni nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: D band at ~1350 cm^{-1} and G band at ~1583 cm^{-1} confirm porous carbon matrix; I_D/I_G values are 0.86, 0.91, 0.94, 0.96, and 0.99 for Ni/C, Cu/C, Ni_{0.75}Cu_{0.25}/C, Ni_{0.50}Cu_{0.50}/C, and Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two characteristic peaks at ∼1350 and ∼1583 cm−1 were observed in all the samples that correspond to the D and G bands of the porous carbon matrix, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C shows better thermal stability than monometallic counterparts with metal content of 79.39, 87.98, and 91.75 wt% for Cu/C, Ni/C, and Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The metal content was found to be 79.39, 87.98, and 91.75% (wt %) for Cu/C, Ni/C, and Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C electrocatalysts from the TGA analysis, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C shows type II isotherm characteristic of mesoporous materials with BET surface area of 157 m²g^{-1}, pore volume of 0.31 cm³g^{-1}, and average pore size of 7.74 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The BET surface area of Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C was found to be 157 m²g^{-1}. ... The pore volume was found to be 0.31 cm³ g^{-1}.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanoparticles uniformly anchored in porous carbon matrix with average particle sizes of 21.04±1.71, 13.86±1.73, 14.51±2.90, 11.58±2.02, and 9.76±2.52 nm for Cu/C, Ni/C, Ni_{0.5}Cu_{0.5}/C, Ni_{0.75}Cu_{0.25}/C, and Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average particle size of the electrocatalysts were determined to be 21.04±1.71, 13.86±1.73, 14.51±2.90, 11.58±2.02, and 9.76±2.52 for the Cu/C, Ni/C, Ni_{0.5}Cu_{0.5}/C, Ni_{0.75}Cu_{0.25}/C, and Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C electrocatalysts, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu NPs well-dispersed in porous carbon with interplanar spacing of ~0.21 nm corresponding to (111) facet of NiCu alloy; HAADF-STEM confirms carbon-wrapped NiCu nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM image also demonstrated that the NPs are highly crystalline as seen in Figure 2F, with an interplanar spacing of ∼0.21 nm that corresponds to the (111) facet of the bimetallic NiCu alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping confirms coexistence and distribution of C, Cu, and Ni elements in Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-based elemental mapping of the Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C confirmed the coexistence and distribution of the C, Cu and Ni elements in the sample (Figure 2H).

nodes.characterization_summary: Detects C K edge (~284 eV), Ni L edge (~855 eV), and Cu L edge (~935 eV) confirming presence of C, Ni, and Cu in Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As seen in Figure 2I, the EELS detected three signals including C K edge (∼284 eV), Ni L edge (∼855 eV) and Cu L edge (∼935 eV) confirming the presence of C, Ni, and Cu.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p_{3/2} binding energy of Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C nanoparticles shifted ~3 times compared to other bimetallic systems (Figure 3F); surface Ni contents are 9.45%, 9.97%, and 5.27% for Ni_{0.75}Cu_{0.25}/C, Ni_{0.50}Cu_{0.50}/C, and Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C respectively (Table S2); C 1s deconvoluted at 284.8, 286.2, 287.8, 289.3 eV (C-C, C-O, O=C-H, O=C-O); O 1s at 530, 531.7, 533.4 eV (O^{2-}, bridging hydroxyls, absorbed water).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the binding energy for Ni 2p_{3/2} band of the Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C nanoparticles were shifted ∼3 times (ΔBE) compared to other bimetallic systems (Figure 3F) ... Ni and Cu contents at the nanoalloy surfaces were estimated from the integrated areas of the Ni 2p and Cu 2p regions (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms presence of Cu, Ni, and C in all bimetallic samples Ni_{0.50}Cu_{0.50}/C, Ni_{0.75}Cu_{0.25}/C, and Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS spectrum and elemental mapping confirmed the presence of Cu, Ni, and C in all bimetallic samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl values measured for ECSA estimation; Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C shows highest C_dl of 1.4 mF·cm^{-2} for OER (factor of 2 higher than other bimetallics) and highest ECSA of ~115 cm^2 for HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl of Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C nanocatalysts surpassed by a factor of 2 than the values of the other bimetallic nanoparticles, reaching 1.4 mF·cm^{-2} (Figure 4C) ... The Ni_{0.25}Cu_{0.75}/C electrocatalyst displayed the highest ECSA of about 115 cm^2.
